correctness.rationale: For T=U|T|, restrict |T| to H_0=N(T)^perp. Its zero spectral projection vanishes. A finite positive Borel quantization of its nonzero spectrum, with all cell diameters below epsilon and the top-cell representative fixed at ||T||, yields an injective positive finite-spectrum A_epsilon of the same norm. Extending by zero gives B with the same support as |T|. Therefore S=UB has |S|=B, the same polar partial isometry U, the same kernel and norm, and distance below epsilon. Lemma 8.1 of arXiv:2609.37621 puts B in beta(H), hence S in beta_0(H). No experiment substitutes for proof.

originality.rationale: The focal proof already implies ordinary beta_0 density because its approximants have finite-spectrum modulus; that corollary is therefore treated as prior coverage. The final claim is strictly stronger: it preserves the original polar partial isometry, kernel, and operator norm simultaneously. Full-text inspection and focused semantic searches did not locate that structured approximation theorem.
